name: The Shore Dogs
description:
The Shore Dogs run a smuggling operation along Lake Michigan's western shore between Milwaukee and Chicago, using a fleet of small watercraft — kayaks, converted fishing boats, and a few stolen corporate speedboats — to move cargo along the coastline outside the range of land-based surveillance. The lake is their highway, and they know its currents, weather patterns, and radar gaps better than anyone.

The crew is about thirty-five strong, based out of a cluster of partially submerged boathouses near Waukegan. Most members come from families that used to work the lake — fishing, shipping, harbor maintenance — before those industries were automated or abandoned. They grew up on the water and they fight on it too. Shore Dog boarding actions against rival boats are fast, brutal, and usually successful.

The Dogs smuggle primarily between Milwaukee and Chicago, serving as a logistics link for gangs and syndicates in both cities. They carry augments, weapons, pharmaceuticals, luxury goods, and occasionally people. Their rates are competitive because their overhead is low — boats don't need roads, and the lake doesn't charge tolls. They also fish, both for food and as cover for their movements. A Shore Dog boat hauling contraband looks identical to a Shore Dog boat hauling walleye until you open the hidden compartments.

The crew maintains a strict internal code: no stealing from clients, no throwing crew overboard, and no running drugs that kill kids. That last rule costs them business but earns them a reputation as relatively principled, for smugglers. They've been known to refuse cargo and even turn in clients who violate their code, which makes them trusted by the factions they work with.
ideology: The lake is free. No corporation owns the water, no security force patrols every mile of shoreline, and the Shore Dogs intend to keep it that way. They're libertarians of the waterways — they believe in free movement, free trade, and the right to make a living without corporate permission.
territory: Lake Michigan's western shoreline from Milwaukee to Chicago. Base of operations in Waukegan's submerged boathouses.
methods: Lakeside smuggling — moving cargo by boat along routes that bypass all land-based checkpoints
Coastal navigation — intimate knowledge of currents, weather, radar gaps, and safe harbors
Boarding actions — fast, aggressive boat-to-boat combat for defense or opportunistic piracy
Fishing cover — legitimate fishing operations that mask smuggling movements
Harbor network — relationships with dock workers and harbor contacts along the entire western shore
Weather exploitation — moving during storms and fog when surveillance is degraded
resources: A fleet of small watercraft modified for speed and concealment
Intimate knowledge of Lake Michigan's western shoreline, currents, and weather patterns
A base in Waukegan's partially submerged boathouses — accessible only by water
Relationships with factions in both Milwaukee and Chicago who need inter-city logistics
Fishing equipment and licenses that provide cover for movement
Thirty-five experienced sailors and fighters comfortable with waterborne operations

story_hooks: A Shore Dog boat disappeared on a routine run — the crew thinks pirates, but the cargo manifest suggests something else
A corporate entity is deploying autonomous patrol boats on the lake, threatening the Dogs' entire operation
The Dogs found a sealed container floating in the lake — its contents are worth a fortune and marked with military insignia
A rival smuggling crew is undercutting the Dogs by running the drugs they refuse to carry — and clients are switching
The Dogs are being pressured to smuggle a person out of Chicago who may be a corporate fugitive or may be a war criminal
